blocks.text: Agents are AI-powered assistants that can understand your goal, decide the next best step, and use connected tools and data sources to complete tasks on your behalf. Unlike a basic chatbot that only answers questions, an agent can take action, such as retrieving information, running checks, generating outputs, and coordinating multistep workflows while keeping you in control.

In Zscaler's AI Security, agents are AI orchestration workflows or chatbots that can connect LLMs, enterprise data sources (knowledge), and tools, including agents to complete tasks or workflows. Because agents can invoke tools and interact with sensitive resources, they are treated as first-class AI assets that need dedicated discovery, inventory, and risk visibility across cloud and code environments.
The AI Assets - Agents page provides the following benefits and enables you to:

blocks.item: Find and inventory agents discovered across environments (e.g., cloud services and code repositories) in one place.
View an agent’s overall risk level, rolled up from its most severe issues, along with warning indicators and Asset Risk labels that flag adverse conditions.
Understand what the agent connects to, such as tools, agents, data sources, and identities with access to estimate potential blast radius.
Prioritize, review and remediate by focusing on agents with the highest-risk issues and broadest access paths.
Support lifecycle decisions based on discovery status and risk.

blocks.heading: About the AI Assets - Agents Page

blocks.text: On the AI Assets - Agents page (AI Infrastructure > AI Assets - Agents), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Filter by Business Units.
View the following widgets for a quick, at-a-glance summary of the agents:
Agents by Risk: View the distribution of agents by severity of risk, categorized as Critical, High, Medium, Low, or Unknown.
Agents by Status: View the distribution of governance status of each agent, categorized as Sanctioned, Unsanctioned, or Pending.
Agents with Access to Sensitive Data: View the number of agents that can access sensitive data and view the number of agents that are publicly exposed.
Search for a specific agent.
Apply filters to view specific data.
View a list of agents which were discovered. For each agent you can view:
Name: The name of the agent. Click the agent's name to view additional details.
General Information: Information such as type, path, source, account ID, account name, organization ID, and region. Click More Details for a graphical view.

Risk Level: Indicates the potential blast radius if this agent is compromised. The rating is based on capabilities such as system command execution, file write or delete access, credential storage or access, and outbound (external) network calls.
Lifecycle: Timeline showing the stages an AI model goes through from discovery to deployment, monitoring, and updates, with timestamps for key milestones.
The detailed information page also displays the following tabs:
Graph View
A graph shows the connections between the agents and associated components. Click the nodes to view additional details of each entity.
Data Security (visible if data is filtered by sensitive data)
Use this tab to view information about the sensitive files that were discovered.
Matched Files: The number of files that matched the DLP engines.
Triggers: Number of alerts raised for the resource.
DLP Engines: The DLP engines that match sensitive records.
DLP Dictionaries: The dictionaries associated with the DLP engines.
Document Categories: The category of document detected in the resource.
Document Types: The number of documents detected in the resource.
You can do the following in the data security table:
Search for a specific sensitive file.
Filter data by Linked Datastore, Sensitive DLP Engines, DLP Engines, DLP Dictionaries, Database, or Document Type.
View a list of sensitive files which were discovered. For each sensitive file you can view:
File Name
File Path
File Size
DLP Engines
DLP Dictionaries
Document Types
Last Completed Scan
Created Date
Issues
Use this tab to view a list of issues that were discovered. For each issue, you can view:
Issue ID: The unique identifier for the issue.
Policy Name: The policy title.
Policy Category: The threat category, e.g., public exposure, data loss, etc., that the policy belongs to.
Risk Level: The risk level, i.e., Critical, High, Medium, or Low.
Cloud Account: The unique identifier of the cloud account in which the model is located.
Created On: The date and time the issue was created.
Last Updated: The date and time the issue was last updated.
Type: The type of server, i.e., Remote or Local.
Risk Level: The risk level of the agent based on the risk score.
Asset Risk: The security posture assigned to the identity (Dormant Identity, MFA Disabled, etc.). Hover over the label to see the description of each posture.
Environment: Indicates where the asset was discovered, e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP, etc.
Source: Indicates the specific location or service where the agent was discovered, stored, or hosted.
Risk Score: Indicates the overall severity rating that indicates how risky a specific agent is. Risk levels are classified as Critical, High, Medium, or Low.
Last Discovered: The timestamp of when the agent was discovered.
Status: The approval status of the agents, e.g., Pending, Sanctioned, or Unsanctioned.
